function.name: search_satellite_imagery
function.description: Search for satellite imagery (Sentinel-2 L2A) over Rwanda or a specific area. Returns available scenes with dates, cloud cover, and download links. Use this when the user asks about satellite images, remote sensing data, or wants to find imagery for a specific date/location.

bbox.description: Bounding box as 'west,south,east,north' in WGS84 coordinates. Defaults to Rwanda bounds if not specified.

datetime_range.description: Date range in ISO 8601 format like '2024-01-01/2024-06-30'. Defaults to last 30 days.

function.name: get_field_health
function.description: Get recent vegetation health statistics for a specific polygon/area from Sentinel-2 L2A (Digital Earth Africa). Returns NDVI (and optionally NDWI, BSI) mean/std/min/max per day for the last 30 days. PREFERRED tool when the user asks about NDVI, crop health, vegetation, or field monitoring for a specific area, buffer zone, field, or any polygon that is NOT an admin boundary. Use the geometry from an existing layer on the map (buffer, drawn polygon, uploaded field boundary). WHEN TO USE: a user-drawn polygon, any geography, optionally a specific date. WHEN NOT TO USE: Rwanda admin boundary (district/sector/cell) — use get_agri_indices. Cached weekly aggregates — use get_ndvi_stats or get_parcel_ndvi_stats.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon geometry of the field to analyse

index.description: Index type: 'ndvi' for NDVI only, 'multi' for NDVI+NDWI+BSI. Default: ndvi

function.name: get_ndvi_stats
function.description: Read the latest NDVI vegetation index statistics for a single Rwanda district. Returns one weekly mean NDVI number. ONLY use for simple single-number NDVI lookups like 'what is the NDVI in Musanze'. Do NOT use for situation overviews, status reports, or assessment questions — use get_insurance_intelligence instead, which combines rainfall + NDVI + ET + dry spells + triggers into one report. WHEN TO USE: one weekly mean NDVI value for ONE named Rwanda district. WHEN NOT TO USE: sector/cell granularity — use get_cell_ndvi_stats. Real-time over a polygon — use get_field_health. User-uploaded field — use get_parcel_ndvi_stats.

district.description: Filter results to a specific district name (e.g. Bugesera, Musanze, Gasabo)

function.name: get_cell_ndvi_stats
function.description: Read NDVI vegetation index statistics at sector or cell level within a district. Returns sector_name and cell_name in every row so results can be grouped by sector. When sector is provided, returns only cells in that sector. When only district is provided, returns all sectors with their cells. Use as a SUPPLEMENT after get_insurance_intelligence when the user wants spatial breakdown. Do NOT use as the primary tool for situation/overview questions. WHEN TO USE: sector- or cell-level NDVI within a named Rwanda district. WHEN NOT TO USE: district-level summary — use get_ndvi_stats. User-uploaded polygon — use get_parcel_ndvi_stats.

cell_name.description: Filter by cell name (partial match supported)

sector.description: Filter by sector name to see all cells within a sector

district.description: Filter by district name to see all sectors and cells within a district

function.name: get_soil_properties
function.description: Query African soil properties at a specific location using iSDAsoil's 30m resolution machine learning predictions. Returns soil pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, organic carbon, clay/sand/silt content, texture class, and 12+ other properties. Each property includes depth (0-20cm or 20-50cm) and uncertainty estimates. Use when the user asks about soil quality, fertility, nutrients, texture, or agronomic suitability at a specific location in Africa.

properties.description: List of soil properties to query. Defaults to 8 most useful for agriculture: ph, nitrogen_total, phosphorous_extractable, potassium_extractable, carbon_organic, clay_content, sand_content, texture_class

depth.description: Soil depth range in centimeters. Default: 0-20

function.name: get_parcel_ndvi_stats
function.description: Read parcel-level NDVI statistics from the nightly cache for user-uploaded field boundaries. Updated nightly by Dagster at 10m native Sentinel-2 resolution. These are individual farm fields uploaded by users and tagged with rwanda_parcels=true. Returns per-parcel mean, std, min, max NDVI and estimated area. Use when the user asks about specific fields, farm parcels, or individual plot vegetation health. WHEN TO USE: user-uploaded field boundary by slug or name (e.g. Cyampirita, Kabarama, Kabari). WHEN NOT TO USE: Rwanda admin boundary — use get_ndvi_stats or get_cell_ndvi_stats. Real-time on an arbitrary polygon — use get_field_health.

parcel_name.description: Filter by parcel/field name (partial match supported)

function.name: get_agri_indices
function.description: Get REAL-TIME agricultural vegetation indices for Rwanda ADMINISTRATIVE BOUNDARIES only (districts, sectors, cells). Computes 6 indices: NDVI, EVI, NDWI, SAVI, NDRE, NDBI. Only use when the user explicitly asks for district/sector/cell level analysis. Do NOT use for custom areas, buffers, fields, or drawn polygons — use get_field_health instead for those. WHEN TO USE: Rwanda ADMIN boundaries (district/sector/cell) needing live multi-index values now. WHEN NOT TO USE: user-drawn polygon — use get_field_health. Pre-aggregated weekly NDVI only — use get_ndvi_stats or get_cell_ndvi_stats.

admin_level.description: Administrative level: 'district' (30 units), 'sector' (416 units, ADM3), 'cell' (2148 units, ADM4). Default: district

name.description: Filter to a specific admin unit name (e.g. 'Gasabo', 'Kimisagara'). Partial match supported.

district.description: Filter sectors/cells within a specific district

function.name: add_land_cover_layer
function.description: Add ESRI 10m Annual LULC 2024 land cover layer to the map. Shows cropland vs non-cropland at 10m resolution from satellite imagery. Two modes: 'all' shows all 9 land cover classes (water, trees, flooded vegetation, crops, built area, bare ground, snow/ice, clouds, rangeland). 'cropland' highlights cropland in green and mutes everything else. IMPORTANT: always clip to the area of interest. Preferred: pass bbox from the relevant layer's bounds in MapState. Alternative: pass lat+lon to auto-detect the correct admin boundary. NEVER guess district names. NEVER show the entire country unless the user explicitly asks for it. WHEN TO USE: the user wants to SEE land cover on the map. WHEN NOT TO USE: numeric land-cover area or percentage for a region — use query_worldcover_stats. This tool only adds a visual layer.

mode.description: Visualization mode: 'all' shows all 9 land cover classes with distinct colours. 'cropland' highlights cropland areas in green and mutes all other classes. Default: all

lat.description: Latitude (EPSG:4326) of the point of interest. The tool auto-detects the containing district/sector/cell from PostGIS for clipping. Use this instead of guessing district names.

lon.description: Longitude (EPSG:4326) of the point of interest.

bbox.description: Bounding box [west, south, east, north] in EPSG:4326 to clip the layer to. Use when the user refers to a custom area (buffer circle, drawn polygon, existing layer extent). Extract the bounds from the relevant layer in MapState.

district.description: Rwanda district name — only use if the user explicitly names a district. Prefer lat/lon or bbox instead.

sector.description: Rwanda sector name — only use if the user explicitly names a sector.

cell.description: Rwanda cell name — only use if the user explicitly names a cell.

function.name: query_worldcover_stats
function.description: Query ESRI 10m LULC 2024 land-cover statistics for a specific area. Two query types: 'land_cover' returns area in hectares for each land-cover class (crops, trees, rangeland, etc.). 'largest_cropland' returns the biggest contiguous cropland plantations ranked by area. IMPORTANT: always scope to the user's area of interest. Preferred: pass bbox from the relevant layer's bounds in MapState. Alternative: pass lat+lon from the Center Point layer — the tool will auto-detect the correct admin boundary. NEVER guess district names — use bbox or lat/lon and let the tool resolve the location.

query_type.description: land_cover: area breakdown by land-cover class (DEFAULT). largest_cropland: ranked list of biggest contiguous cropland areas.

lat.description: Latitude (EPSG:4326) of the point of interest. The tool auto-detects the containing district/sector/cell from PostGIS. Use this instead of guessing district names.

lon.description: Longitude (EPSG:4326) of the point of interest.

bbox.description: Bounding box [west, south, east, north] in EPSG:4326. Use when the user refers to a custom area (buffer circle, drawn polygon, existing layer extent). Extract the bounds from the relevant layer in MapState. This performs on-the-fly analysis for the exact area.

district.description: Rwanda district name — only use if the user explicitly names a district. Prefer lat/lon or bbox instead.

sector.description: Rwanda sector name — only use if the user explicitly names a sector.

cell.description: Rwanda cell name — only use if the user explicitly names a cell.

limit.description: Max results for largest_cropland query. Default: 10

function.name: get_anomaly_alerts
function.description: Read the latest vegetation anomaly alerts. Returns locations where NDVI dropped significantly below normal, indicating crop stress, drought, or disease. Use alongside get_insurance_intelligence for situation overviews — it adds spatial hotspot detail. Also use standalone when the user asks specifically about crop problems, stress alerts, or anomalies.

function.name: get_yield_risk
function.description: Read pre-computed yield risk assessments, refreshed weekly. Uses Mann-Kendall trend analysis and Theil-Sen slope on NDVI time series to flag crop yield risk per district. It is a vegetation trend, not a yield estimate in tonnes; say so when the user asks for a yield forecast. Returns risk level (low/normal/moderate/high/critical), trend direction, and statistical confidence. Use when the user asks about harvest outlook, yield risk, or crop risk.

function.name: get_drought_status
function.description: Read pre-computed drought status, refreshed weekly. Uses Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) with NDWI water stress analysis per district. Returns drought status (normal/watch/moderate_drought/severe_drought), VCI score, and affected period count. Use when the user asks about drought, water stress, or dry conditions. WHEN TO USE: drought severity now (VCI + NDWI). WHEN NOT TO USE: forward-looking yield risk — use get_yield_risk. Recent NDVI drop alerts — use get_anomaly_alerts. Historical no-rain windows — use detect_dry_spells.

function.name: get_crop_growth_stage
function.description: Read pre-computed crop growth stage analysis, refreshed weekly. Uses NDVI phenology curve analysis to identify current crop stage per district: dormant, green_up, peak, senescence, or harvest. Returns current stage, peak NDVI date, and key phenological transition dates. Use when the user asks about crop growth, planting, harvesting, or growing season.

function.name: get_weather_stats
function.description: Read daily weather statistics from the PostgreSQL cache. Data comes from Copernicus AgERA5 agrometeorological indicators at 0.1° (~10km) grid resolution, aggregated to district level. Returns daily temperature (mean/max/min °C), precipitation (mm/day), and solar radiation (MJ/m²/day). NOTE: Results are district-level averages. Actual conditions vary within a district due to elevation, terrain, and microclimates. For location-specific weather, use get_forecast with exact lat/lon instead. Use this tool for HISTORICAL weather only.

district.description: Filter to a specific district name (e.g. Bugesera, Musanze, Gasabo)

date_from.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: 30 days ago)

date_to.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: today)

function.name: get_forecast
function.description: Get weather forecast for any location in Rwanda. Fuses 4 models — ECMWF IFS (9km), GFS (13km), ICON (11km), GraphCast AI (28km) — for consensus forecasts with risk assessment. Returns daily temperature, precipitation, wind, ET0, soil moisture, and a natural-language risk briefing. Each location gets unique interpolated values (sector-level precision). Use when the user asks about weather forecast, future weather, expected rainfall, upcoming conditions, or any forward-looking weather question.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location (e.g. -1.9403 for Kigali)

longitude.description: Longitude of the location (e.g. 29.8739 for Kigali)

district.description: Rwanda district name — will use district centroid if lat/lon not provided

forecast_days.description: Number of days to forecast (1-16, default 10)

function.name: get_forecast_accuracy
function.description: Compare weather forecast against observed AgERA5 weather data to measure accuracy. Returns MAE (Mean Absolute Error) and bias for temperature and precipitation across districts where both forecast and observation exist. Use when the user asks about forecast accuracy, model performance, how good the forecast is, or weather prediction quality.

district.description: Specific district to check accuracy for (optional — defaults to all districts)

lookback_days.description: Number of days to look back for accuracy comparison. Default: 30

function.name: get_soil_moisture
function.description: Query relative soil moisture from FAO WaPOR v3 at 100m dekadal (10-day) resolution. Returns a time series of soil moisture percentage for the given location. Use when the user asks about soil moisture, soil wetness, soil dryness, irrigation needs, or water availability in the soil. WHEN TO USE: WaPOR 100m dekadal (10-day) area-aggregated soil moisture, optical-derived. WHEN NOT TO USE: soil texture/chemistry — use get_soil_properties.

function.name: get_evapotranspiration
function.description: Query actual evapotranspiration (ET) and optionally transpiration and net primary productivity from FAO WaPOR v3 at 100m dekadal (10-day) resolution. Returns a time series of ET values in mm/day for the given location. Use when the user asks about evapotranspiration, water use, crop water consumption, water productivity, ET, or how much water a crop/field is using.

include_components.description: If true, also return transpiration and net primary productivity. Default: false

function.name: detect_dry_spells
function.description: Detect historical dry spells from observed weather data (AgERA5). Scans for consecutive days where precipitation was below a threshold. Use when the user asks about dry spells, drought events, consecutive dry days, rainfall gaps, or historical drought periods for Rwanda districts.

district.description: District name to filter (e.g. Gasabo, Bugesera). Optional — defaults to all districts

threshold_mm.description: Daily precipitation threshold in mm — days below this count as dry. Default: 2.0

min_duration_days.description: Minimum consecutive dry days to qualify as a dry spell. Default: 10

function.name: get_insurance_accuracy
function.description: Compute weather data accuracy for agricultural insurance underwriting. Returns binary rainfall detection metrics (POD, FAR, HSS, CSI), dry spell detection results, NDVI-weather concordance, and an overall confidence rating (0-100). Use when the user asks about insurance accuracy, weather data reliability, rainfall detection quality, underwriting confidence, or whether weather data is good enough for crop insurance.

district.description: District name (e.g. Gasabo, Bugesera). Optional — defaults to all districts

season.description: Rwanda growing season: A (Sep-Jan) or B (Feb-Jun). Optional — defaults to last 90 days

threshold_mm.description: Rainfall threshold in mm for binary rain/no-rain classification. Default: 5.0

function.name: get_insurance_intelligence
function.description: Get a comprehensive agricultural situation report for any location in Rwanda. This is the PRIMARY tool for any question about the 'situation', 'status', 'overview', 'how is [place] doing', or 'what's happening in [place]'. Combines rainfall (CHIRPS cumulative + SPI drought index), vegetation health (NDVI + Sentinel-1 SAR), evapotranspiration (WaPOR), soil moisture, dry spells, season progress, parametric trigger thresholds, and multi-model forecast outlook (ECMWF IFS + GFS + ICON + GraphCast) into one unified report. Reports are location-based (not crop-specific) — they show weather and vegetation conditions for the area regardless of what is planted. Supports 4 audience views: farmer (simple), insurance (trigger table), agronomist (technical + recommendations), scientist (full methodology). Works at any admin level: district, sector, cell, or village. COMPARISON MODE: when the user asks to compare areas (e.g. 'compare sectors in Nyamasheke', 'which districts get more rain', 'difference between sectors'), set compare_level to the level being compared. This returns ALL signals for every child area in one call. IMPORTANT: at least one location parameter (district, sector, cell, or village) is required. WHEN TO USE: open-ended 'what is happening here' / 'how is this farm doing' over a Rwanda location — fuses NDVI + weather + drought + crop into one report. WHEN NOT TO USE: the user asked one narrow question (just rainfall, just NDVI, just soil) — call the specific tool. Do NOT default to this for every Rwanda question.

crop.description: Optional crop name if the user explicitly mentions one. The report shows location-based conditions (rainfall, NDVI, soil moisture, etc) regardless — we cannot detect what crop is planted from satellite. Leave empty or omit for general location reports.

season.description: Growing season: A (Sep-Feb) or B (Feb-Jul). Auto-detected if omitted

sector.description: Sector name within a district (e.g. Kinigi, Kimironko)

village.description: Village name — most specific admin level

audience.description: Who is reading this report: farmer (plain words, rain compared with usual), insurance (trigger table with evidence), agronomist (indices and recommendations), scientist (all numbers and methods). Set it ONLY when the user asks for a particular view (for example: explain it for a farmer); otherwise omit it and the saved role of the user is used

compare_level.description: COMPARISON MODE: set this to compare all child areas at this admin level. 'sector' with district=X compares all sectors in district X. 'cell' with sector=Y compares all cells in sector Y. 'district' compares all 30 districts nationwide. Returns rainfall, SPI, NDVI, soil moisture, ET, temperature, SAR, and dry spells for every area. Only set this when the user asks to COMPARE areas — omit for single-location reports.

function.name: detect_flood_extent
function.description: Delineate flood extent by comparing Sentinel-1 SAR radar imagery from before and after a flood event. Returns new flood area (excluding permanent water bodies) with polygons suitable for insurance claim validation.

function.name: search_brain
function.description: Search the knowledge brain for entities and information. Uses hybrid search (keyword + vector) across brain pages. Returns ranked results with compiled truth summaries. Use when the user asks about a field, farmer, district, claim, policy, or any entity the brain might know about.

type.description: Filter by page type: field, farmer, district, company, insurance_worker, claim, policy, season, crop, weather_station, equipment

function.name: get_entity
function.description: Get a specific brain page by its slug. Returns the full compiled truth, recent timeline entries, tags, and linked entities. Use when the user asks about a specific known entity like 'field-gasabo-001' or 'farmer-uwimana'.

function.name: brain_graph_query
function.description: Walk the Brain's links from one entity: the related entities up to N hops out, each link with its type (field_in_district, field_owned_by, claim_under_policy, crop_planted_in, ...). Use for RELATIONAL questions: 'which fields are under this policy', 'claims in this district last season', 'who owns the fields in Huye', 'what is Cyampirita connected to'. For a plain lookup use search_brain first to find the slug; for how one value changed over time use brain_trajectory.

slug.description: Starting entity slug, e.g. 'fields/cyampirita', 'districts/huye'. Use search_brain to find it if unsure.

depth.description: Hops out from the starting entity (default 2, limited to 1-5).

edge_types.description: Optional: only these link types, e.g. ['field_in_district', 'policy_covers_field'].

function.name: brain_trajectory
function.description: History of one recorded value on one Brain entity, oldest to newest, with drops flagged as regressions. Use for 'how has the NDVI of field X changed', 'soil moisture history for this farm'. Common keys: ndvi, soil_moisture, anomaly_score, crop, yield_kg_per_ha. Returns entries with valid_from, value, status and regression_flag.

slug.description: Entity slug, e.g. 'fields/cyampirita'. Use search_brain to find it if unsure.

function.name: add_observation
function.description: Add a timeline observation to a brain page. Use when the user reports a field visit, observation, measurement, or event that should be recorded in an entity's history. The brain grows with every observation.

slug.description: The entity slug to add the observation to

date.description: Date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: today

function.name: search_location
function.description: Search for a location by name and return its bounding box and coordinates. Use this when the user mentions a place name and you need geographic coordinates for satellite imagery or spectral index tools.

query.description: Place name to search for, e.g. 'Musanze district, Rwanda' or 'Kigali'

function.name: display_satellite_layer
function.description: Display satellite imagery (true color) on the map for a specific area and date range. Searches Earth Search for the best Sentinel-2 scene and adds it as a visible tile layer. Use this when the user wants to SEE satellite imagery on the map for a location.

bbox.description: Bounding box as 'west,south,east,north' in WGS84 coordinates, e.g. '29.44,-1.72,29.68,-1.50'

date_from.description: Start date in ISO 8601 format, e.g. '2025-01-01'

date_to.description: End date in ISO 8601 format, e.g. '2025-01-31'

layer_name.description: Display name for the map layer, e.g. 'Musanze TCI Jan 2025'

function.name: compute_spectral_index
function.description: Compute a spectral index (NDVI, NDWI, or NBR) over an area and display it on the map with a colormap. Returns area statistics (mean, std, min, max). Use this for vegetation health analysis (NDVI), water/flood detection (NDWI), or burn severity mapping (NBR). Always call search_location first to get the bbox. WHEN TO USE: the user wants to SEE NDVI/NDWI/NBR as a coloured layer on the map. WHEN NOT TO USE: numbers/stats only — use get_field_health or get_ndvi_stats. This tool renders; it does not return tabular metrics.

bbox.description: Bounding box as 'west,south,east,north' in WGS84 coordinates

index.description: Spectral index to compute: 'ndvi' (vegetation health), 'ndwi' (water/flooding), or 'nbr' (burn severity)

date_from.description: Start date in ISO 8601 format, e.g. '2025-01-01'

date_to.description: End date in ISO 8601 format, e.g. '2025-01-31'

layer_name.description: Display name for the map layer, e.g. 'NDVI Musanze Jan 2025'
